text:
Stellantis Surges 10% on Reaffirmed Guidance and Accelerating Cost Savings; Ford Inches Higher, General Motors and Tesla Hold Steady
Stellantis is surging while its Detroit rivals barely twitch, but a brutal cash flow miss and mounting European losses raise the question of whether this relief rally has any real foundation beneath it.
A confirmed 2026 outlook and a cost-cutting program that’s gaining speed are sending Stellantis (NYSE:STLA | STLA Price Prediction) sharply higher, even as its Detroit rivals barely move. Stellantis stock sits at $4.57 early in the session, up 10%.
Checking in on the peers, Ford Motor (NYSE:F) stock trails Stellantis at $12, up 0.7%. General Motors (NYSE:GM) stock is at $81, up 0.3%.
Stellantis Holds Its 2026 Guidance as Cost Savings Speed Up
On October 28, Stellantis disclosed its Q3 2026 net revenues of €37.6 billion, up 1% from a year earlier. Stellantis’s net loss narrowed sharply to €453 million, far smaller than the loss it posted in the year-earlier quarter. That mix of barely higher sales and much smaller losses points to a recovery built on cost discipline more than volume.
Adjusted operating income at Stellantis rose to €256 million from €90 million a year earlier, and the company’s margin improved to 0.7% from 0.2%. Chief executive Antonio Filosa reaffirmed Stellantis’s 2026 guidance, along with its expectation of positive industrial free cash flow in 2027. Holding that outlook answers the biggest question Stellantis faced heading into the report.
Antonio Filosa said Stellantis remains on track. The company aims to implement at least 40% of the €6 billion run-rate efficiency target in its Value Creation Program by year-end. Bloomberg reported that Stellantis guided savings from the overhaul to as much as €600 million in Q4 2026, up from roughly €300 million in Q3. Accelerating savings could give Stellantis a buffer as raw material costs climb.
North America swung back to profit. Stellantis posted an adjusted operating profit of €64 million, reversing a year-earlier loss, helped by new models such as the Ram 1500 Hemi and the Jeep Cherokee hybrid. Ram 1500 U.S. sales at Stellantis jumped 73% from a year earlier. Tariffs are biting less, too, with Stellantis now estimating full-year net tariff expense at about €1 billion, below its prior estimate of as much as €1.2 billion.
Stellantis Moves Apart From Detroit as Europe and Cash Flow Lag
Europe was the weak spot. Stellantis’s Enlarged Europe region swung to an adjusted operating loss of €311 million on lower prices and a shift toward less-profitable electric vehicles. Competition from Chinese makers such as BYD, along with Volkswagen and Renault, kept pressure on Stellantis in the region. Heavy European exposure sets Stellantis apart from Ford and General Motors, whose profits lean on U.S. trucks and SUVs backed by in-house lending arms.
Cash was the bigger concern, as Stellantis posted industrial free cash flow of negative €4 billion, missing analyst expectations, according to Bloomberg. Citi analyst Harald Hendrikse called it “very weak.” He wrote that “the key question remains how” Stellantis will improve profitability in North America and Europe, adding “we don’t believe that product will be enough.” Management at Stellantis also noted incremental cost headwinds from memory chips and recalls in Q4.
Detroit’s automakers are barely moving by comparison, and the sector’s electric vehicle leader is just as calm. Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock is at $409, up 0.5%. Ford stock is down 7% year to date (YTD), and Tesla stock is down 9% over the same stretch.
General Motors stock is essentially flat YTD. Stellantis stock, by contrast, is down 58% YTD, a far deeper slide that helps explain the size of the relief move.
Stellantis Turnaround Faces Its Next Tests
Stellantis will soon find out whether Value Creation Program savings actually double in Q4 as guided. Dealer inventory is another marker, with Stellantis ending September at 368,000 U.S. units and 84 days of supply, an improvement from June. Reaching the 320,000 to 350,000 units Stellantis expects by year-end could ease discounting pressure, while a miss could keep dealer lots full into 2027.
Europe’s losses are the swing factor. Stability there could strengthen the bull case for Stellantis while deeper losses would support Citi’s view that new products alone may fall short. More detail on the FaSTLAne 2030 plan could come at Stellantis’s Maserati Day event in Modena on December 10. Auto loan rates could also shape car demand for Stellantis and its rivals, with the Federal Reserve’s policy decision due October 28. A conservative approach could make sense while the debate over Stellantis’s cash flow plays out.
